issue.title: A RUNNING claim row with any unrecognized trailing part is silently dropped by WorkspaceClaimLine::parse, so the allocator hands that workspace to a second agent
issue.description:
Found by the sase-q0 land agent (epic "Guarantee one agent per workspace") while verifying that epic. Originally proposed as a PROPOSED FOLLOW-UP on phase bead sase-q0.2.

`WorkspaceClaimLine::parse` in sase-core (`crates/sase_core/src/agent_launch/mod.rs`) drops an ENTIRE RUNNING-field claim row whenever any trailing pipe-separated part is neither the literal `PINNED` nor a shape `is_timestamp_part` recognizes:

```rust
for part in parts.iter().skip(4) {
    if *part == "PINNED" { pinned = true; }
    else if is_timestamp_part(part) { artifacts_timestamp = Some(...); }
    else { return None; }        // <-- whole row silently discarded
}
```

`is_timestamp_part` (same file, ~line 2276) accepts exactly two shapes: 14 bare digits (`20260818120000`) and 13 chars `YYMMDD_HHMMSS` (`260818_120000`). It rejects the very similar `YYYYMMDD_HHMMSS` (`20260818_120000`), which is the format `%Y%m%d_%H%M%S` produced elsewhere in the sase repo.

This fails OPEN, which is the dangerous direction:
- `list_workspace_claims_from_content` omits the row, so `allocate_and_claim_workspace_from_content` sees that workspace number as free.
- `plan_claim_workspace_from_content`'s "workspace #N is already claimed" guard also parses through `WorkspaceClaimLine::parse`, so it does not reject the second claim either.

Net effect: one unparseable claim row hands a live agent's workspace to a second agent. That is exactly the failure mode epic sase-q0 exists to prevent, and it matches the epic plan's explicit open anomaly ("Either a row was lost from the ProjectSpec file ... or the interleaving differs from the reconstruction"). The epic plan put ProjectSpec-format work out of scope and directed that this be filed as a task rather than widening the epic.

No producer in the sase repo is known to emit a non-conforming trailing part today (all writers go through the Rust `to_line()`), so this is currently latent — but a hand edit, a plugin, or a future field addition turns it into silent double allocation with no error anywhere.

SUGGESTED FIX (judgment needed, not a blind change): make an unrecognized trailing part non-fatal — keep the row, preserve the unknown part verbatim on rewrite, and ignore it for semantics — so an unparseable extra can never make a claimed workspace look free. Optionally widen `is_timestamp_part` to accept `YYYYMMDD_HHMMSS`. Add Rust unit tests that a row with an unknown trailing part is still returned by `list_workspace_claims_from_content` and still blocks `plan_claim_workspace_from_content`.

task_type_fields.impact: Fails open: an unparseable claim row makes a live agent's workspace look free to both allocate_and_claim_workspace_from_content and the already-claimed guard in plan_claim_workspace_from_content, reproducing the exact double-allocation incident epic sase-q0 was created to prevent. Latent today (no known producer of a non-conforming part), but silent and unbounded when triggered.
task_type_fields.repro:
In the sase-core checkout (`sase repo open sase-core`), add to `crates/sase_core/src/agent_launch/mod.rs` tests:

```rust
let content = "RUNNING:\n  #7 | 4242 | ace(run) | mycl | 20260818_120000\n";
assert_eq!(list_workspace_claims_from_content(content).len(), 1); // FAILS: returns 0
```

`20260818_120000` is 15 chars (`%Y%m%d_%H%M%S`), so `is_timestamp_part` returns false and `WorkspaceClaimLine::parse` hits its `else { return None }` branch, discarding the whole row. The same content fed to `plan_claim_workspace_from_content` with `workspace_num: 7` succeeds instead of reporting "workspace #7 is already claimed".

payload.entry: RELATED: sase-q0 — epic 'Guarantee one agent per workspace'. This is the same failure mode (two agents in one checkout) reached through a different door; the epic plan explicitly scoped ProjectSpec-format work out and directed that it be filed as a task. Fixing this closes the plan's stated open anomaly about a claim row appearing lost.

payload.close_reason: Fixed in sase-core. crates/sase_core/src/agent_launch/mod.rs:4408-4426: the trailing-part loop no longer returns None on an unrecognized part -- it pushes WorkspaceClaimSuffixPart::Unknown and keeps the row, so a RUNNING claim can no longer be silently dropped. is_timestamp_part (line 4530) also now accepts the 15-char YYYYMMDD_HHMMSS shape the bead reported as rejected, alongside the 14-digit and 13-char YYMMDD_HHMMSS forms. Verified 2026-08-24 by opening sase-core through /sase_repo.
